verdict.rationale: Docs confirm automatic daily backups for paid plans (supabase-docs-11) and a branching feature for spinning off preview environments from the main project (supabase-docs-26, supabase-docs-36), but neither is documented as true point-in-time recovery (restoring to an arbitrary timestamp) for undoing bad writes. A community report even suggests Supabase historically relied on nightly pg_dump backups rather than continuous PITR, with the CEO only saying they'd 'investigate moving users to PITR' (supabase-comm-4), casting doubt on granular any-point-in-time restore. missing for 10: explicit PITR documentation with retention-window granularity, evidence that branching can be anchored to a specific past timestamp, and independent confirmation that recovery actually works as claimed.
